topic: Free AI IDE Comparison 2026: Trae, Cursor Free, Copilot Free, and Eclipse Theia
summary: Free AI coding options in 2026 split into three practical categories: limited proprietary free tiers (Cursor Hobby and GitHub Copilot Free), subsidized low-cost IDE tiers with a free baseline or trial (Trae), and open-source/BYOK control (Eclipse Theia AI). The best recommendation depends less on raw coding quality and more on whether the reader values zero setup, agent depth, privacy/control, or predictable usage limits.

tools_compared.name: Trae
tools_compared.positioning: AI-native IDE from ByteDance with a free baseline and low-cost Lite/Pro tiers.
tools_compared.free_or_low_cost_offer: Official pricing page lists a Free plan with limited monthly basic usage, Lite at $3/month, Pro with a 7-day free trial then $10/month, Pro+ at $30/month, and Ultra usage tiers.
strengths: Aggressive pricing relative to Cursor and Copilot Pro tiers.
Unlimited autocomplete starts on paid Lite and above.
SOLO mode is included on Lite and Pro tiers.
Cloud task concurrency is explicit: up to 2 concurrent tasks on Lite and up to 10 on Pro.
Good angle for budget-conscious developers who want an IDE-style AI experience rather than a plugin.
limitations: Free tier is limited usage, not an unlimited free IDE-agent plan.
Official pricing shifted from early 'completely free' messaging to a tiered plan model, so older articles may be stale.
Enterprise trust, compliance, and long-term pricing predictability are less proven than GitHub Copilot or Theia's open-source route.
tools_compared.best_for: Developers who want the most featureful AI-native editor experience at the lowest paid price and can tolerate a newer vendor/pricing model.

tools_compared.name: Cursor Free
tools_compared.positioning: AI-first VS Code-derived editor with a free Hobby tier and paid Individual/Teams/Enterprise plans.
tools_compared.free_or_low_cost_offer: Cursor's official pricing page lists Hobby as free with no credit card required, limited Agent requests, and limited Tab completions. Individual starts at $20/month.
strengths: Strongest brand association with AI-native editing and multi-file agent workflows.
Free tier is good for evaluating Cursor UX without a credit card.
Paid Individual includes extended Agent limits, frontier models, MCPs, skills, hooks, cloud agents, and Bugbot usage-based billing.
Teams plan adds centralized billing, team marketplace, shared team context, analytics, privacy mode, and SSO.
Cursor is SOC 2 certified according to its pricing page footer.
limitations: Free plan is intentionally limited and will not satisfy daily agent-heavy use.
Paid plan starts at twice Copilot Pro's listed entry price.
Usage-based pricing requires writers to explain credits and on-demand overage carefully.
tools_compared.best_for: Developers evaluating an AI-native editor and teams likely to upgrade for serious agent work.

tools_compared.name: GitHub Copilot Free
tools_compared.positioning: Free tier of the most widely adopted AI coding assistant, integrated into VS Code and other IDEs.
tools_compared.free_or_low_cost_offer: Official GitHub pricing lists Free at $0 with 2,000 completions per month, access to models such as Haiku 4.5 and GPT-5 mini, Copilot CLI, and no credit card. GitHub's FAQ also states Free users are limited to 2,000 completions and 50 chat requests including Copilot Edits.
strengths: Lowest-friction option for VS Code users and GitHub-centric workflows.
Works beyond VS Code: official page lists Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, Vim, Neovim, JetBrains IDEs, Azure Data Studio, terminals via GitHub CLI, and Windows Terminal Canary chat integration.
Free tier includes a clear monthly completion quota.
Pro is inexpensive at $10/user/month and includes unlimited code completion, next edit suggestions, cloud agent/code review access, third-party agents, model selection, and monthly credits.
Business and Enterprise plans bring organization controls, policy management, and IP indemnity.
limitations: Free tier has a hard chat/edit cap and limited feature depth.
Copilot Free/Pro/Pro+ interactions may be used to train and improve GitHub AI models unless users opt out, according to the official pricing FAQ.
Agent-heavy or premium model workflows are increasingly tied to GitHub AI Credits and usage-based billing.
tools_compared.best_for: Beginners, occasional AI coding users, GitHub-first developers, and teams that need broad IDE compatibility.

tools_compared.name: Eclipse Theia AI / Theia IDE
tools_compared.positioning: Open-source, vendor-neutral AI-native IDE and platform for desktop and cloud tools.
tools_compared.free_or_low_cost_offer: Theia is positioned as an open-source alternative to GitHub Copilot and Cursor. It lets users choose cloud, self-hosted, or local models, tailor prompts, build custom agents, and keep ownership of data. The cost depends on the selected model/provider rather than a bundled SaaS subscription.
strengths: Open-source and vendor-neutral.
Not a VS Code fork, while still using some shared components such as Monaco and supporting the VS Code extension ecosystem through Open VSX.
Strong privacy/control story: customize AI interactions, prompts, models, and agents.
Better fit for enterprises building custom IDEs or regulated workflows where data ownership and transparent AI behavior matter.
Theia AI is a framework for building AI-native desktop and cloud tools, not only an end-user code editor.
limitations: Not a turnkey free cloud-model subscription; model/API costs are external.
Requires more setup and decision-making than Copilot Free or Cursor Hobby.
Consumer mindshare is lower than Cursor and Copilot, so writers should position it as 'best for control' rather than 'best for instant productivity.'
tools_compared.best_for: Developers and organizations that want open-source control, BYOK/local model flexibility, and the option to build custom AI IDE workflows.

key_points: Official Theia positioning: AI-native, open-source, desktop and cloud IDE.

Users can choose cloud, self-hosted, or local models and customize prompts, AI interactions, and custom agents.

facts: Trae Free has limited monthly basic usage.
Trae Lite costs $3/month and includes $5 basic usage plus bonus usage, unlimited autocomplete, SOLO mode, and up to 2 concurrent cloud tasks.
Trae Pro has a 7-day free trial, then $10/month, with $20 basic usage plus bonus usage, unlimited autocomplete, SOLO mode, and up to 10 concurrent cloud tasks.
Trae Pro+ costs $30/month and offers 3.5x more usage than Pro and up to 15 concurrent cloud tasks.
Cursor Hobby is free, requires no credit card, and includes limited Agent requests and limited Tab completions.
Cursor Individual starts at $20/month and includes extended Agent limits, frontier models, MCPs, skills, hooks, cloud agents, and Bugbot on usage-based billing.
Cursor Teams costs $40/user/month and adds team billing/admin, team marketplace, shared context, analytics, privacy mode, and SAML/OIDC SSO.

Cursor Enterprise is custom priced and adds pooled usage, repository/model/MCP controls, auto-run/browser/network controls, audit logs, service accounts, AI code tracking API, priority support, and account management.
GitHub Copilot Free costs $0 and includes 2,000 completions per month, access to selected models, Copilot CLI, and no credit card requirement.
GitHub Copilot Free users are limited to 2,000 completions and 50 chat requests including Copilot Edits.

GitHub Copilot Pro costs $10/user/month and includes unlimited code completion and next edit suggestions, cloud agent and code review access, third-party agents such as Claude Code and Codex, model selection, and $15 monthly total credits.
GitHub Copilot Pro+ costs $39/user/month and includes access to premium models, audit logs, 4x+ included usage vs Pro, and $70 monthly total credits.
GitHub Copilot Max costs $100/user/month for sustained high-volume agent workflows and includes $100/month in GitHub AI Credits.
Copilot supports VS Code, Visual Studio, Vim, Neovim, JetBrains IDEs, Azure Data Studio, GitHub CLI terminal use, and Windows Terminal Canary chat integration.
Theia IDE is an AI-native, modern, open-source development environment for desktop and cloud.
Theia is an open alternative to GitHub Copilot and Cursor and is not a VS Code fork.
Theia supports more than 3,000 extensions through Open VSX.
Theia allows users to choose cloud, self-hosted, or local models, tailor prompts, create custom agents, and maintain data ownership.
Theia AI is an open framework, part of the Theia Platform, for building custom AI-native cloud and desktop tools and IDEs.
The AI-powered Theia IDE is an open, flexible, transparent AI coding tool based on Theia AI.

Trae Lite costs $3/month, Pro costs $10/month after a 7-day free trial, and Pro+ costs $30/month.
Trae Lite includes up to 2 concurrent cloud tasks; Trae Pro includes up to 10 concurrent cloud tasks; Trae Pro+ includes up to 15 concurrent cloud tasks.
Theia IDE supports more than 3,000 extensions through Open VSX.
Theia is explicitly positioned as not a VS Code fork, despite incorporating shared components such as Monaco.
GitHub Copilot claims users report up to 75% higher job satisfaction and up to 55% productivity improvement for writing code.
Copilot Free, Pro, and Pro+ interactions may be used to train and improve GitHub AI models starting April 24 unless users opt out.

angles: Free is not one thing: compare hard caps, queues, external API costs, and open-source setup burden.
Best zero-friction pick: GitHub Copilot Free for beginners and existing VS Code/GitHub users.
Best AI-native editor trial: Cursor Free, but expect serious users to hit limits and upgrade.
Best budget paid bridge: Trae Lite/Pro undercuts Cursor while offering IDE-level AI workflows.
Best control and privacy story: Eclipse Theia AI with BYOK, local/self-hosted models, customizable prompts, and open-source governance.
Free tiers are lead-gen funnels; Theia is the only option here where the IDE/platform itself is open-source and vendor-neutral.
Usage-based billing is the new hidden variable: explain included credits, overages, model access, and what happens after limits.
Theia is not a Copilot-style bundled assistant; position it as an open framework/IDE for teams that want to own the stack.
Cursor vs Copilot Free is editor depth vs ecosystem reach: Cursor wins if you want agentic IDE UX, Copilot wins if you want compatibility and a clear quota.
Trae's story changed: older 'free Cursor alternative' content should be updated to reflect Lite, Pro, Pro+, and Ultra tiers.
